body:
Replace the current hand-rolled C#-specific generator model with a neutral API model and open-ended emitter abstraction.

## Motivation

The generator should model Neovim RPC/API semantics, not C# method declarations. This enables cleaner C# emission, future F# emission, better type mapping, and better generated documentation.

## Scope

- Introduce a neutral generator model:
  - API functions
  - API parameters
  - API types
  - API events
  - documentation
  - version/deprecation metadata
  - request/response specs
  - encoder/decoder specs
- Introduce emitter abstraction:
  - `IApiEmitter`
  - `GeneratedFile`
  - `GeneratedFileSet`
- Move C#-specific concerns into a C# emitter that uses Roslyn to build the AST.
- Avoid Roslyn leaking into the neutral model.
- Preserve current generated output shape as much as practical for the first pass.
- Move the generator to a **separate library** from the CLI tool. The internals stand on their own and shouldn't be tightly-coupled to it exposing a cli tool.

## Out of scope

- F# emitter.
- Major client API redesign.
- Plugin SDK redesign.
- Namespace/package renames unless required internally.

## Acceptance criteria

- Generator core no longer depends on C#-specific declaration models as the shared abstraction.
- Emitter abstraction exists.
- Existing C# generation is implemented through the emitter abstraction.
- Golden tests cover generated output.
- Neutral model has unit coverage.
- CSharpier formats generated C# output.

## Blocked by

- #27 
- #28 
- #29 
- #30 

## Architecture
```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph Core["Nvim.Client.Generator"]
        direction TB

        Ingest["Neovim API ingestion"]
        Model["Neutral API model"]
        Emit["Emitter abstraction"]
        CSharp["C# emitter using Roslyn"]
        Future["Future emitters"]

        Ingest --> Model
        Model --> Emit
        Emit --> CSharp
        Emit -.-> Future
    end

    subgraph CLI["Nvim.Client.Generator.Cli"]
        direction TB

        Args["Parse command/options"]
        Wire["Wire inputs to generator core"]
        Write["Write generated files"]
        Diagnostics["Return diagnostics/exit code"]

        Args --> Wire
        Wire --> Core
        Core --> Write
        Write --> Diagnostics
    end
```

Well, it's more like a design constraint that I think is very important for these clients. They end up being more useful if they are tiny because:

- the surface area is easier for users to understand
- they actually get maintained instead of bit-rotting
- they avoid a bunch of dumb half-working features

I have consolidated #31, #35, and #40 into one breaking replacement rather than maintaining the current split architecture through sequential migrations.

## Product boundary

- One packable project/package/assembly: `Nvim.Client`.
- One public partial client type: `Nvim.Client.NvimClient`.
- No compatibility projects, forwarding namespaces, deprecated newest-generation API, or parallel old/new runtime.
- Generator library, generator CLI, and tests remain repository-internal and non-packable. Publishing/version alignment/nightly generation remain in #36.

The generator and CLI have a hard 2,000-production-line ceiling, targeting 1,400–1,800. Handwritten runtime code must be smaller than the current combined runtime/API baseline.

## Runtime and lifecycle

`NvimClient` will expose borrowed stream/process/stdio attachment, owned synchronous `Start`, owned `ConnectAsync` for TCP/Unix sockets/Windows pipes, raw request/notification operations, async request/notification/UI registrations, `Completion`, `StopAsync`, and `IDisposable`.

The runtime uses MessagePack 3.1.8 low-level reader/writer APIs with untrusted-data security, one receive task, serialized frame writes, atomic request IDs, tracked handler tasks, and one terminal-state transition. It removes `BlockingCollection`, recursive `async void`, `DynamicInvoke`, `ManualResetEvent`, typeless/object-shaped serialization, and indefinite caller requests.

Owned transports/processes are closed deterministically. Supplied streams/processes and stdio remain borrowed. Because an arbitrary borrowed stream read cannot be forcibly cancelled without closing it, stop/dispose settles logical completion without awaiting such a read; any eventual continuation observes terminal state and performs no dispatch or write.

Cancellation cannot tear a MessagePack frame. Pre-write cancellation sends nothing. Post-write request cancellation cancels the caller while retaining correlation so a late response is consumed rather than treated as a protocol fault.

## Wire values and generated API

A closed immutable `NvimValue` hierarchy covers nil, boolean, the complete MessagePack signed/unsigned integer domain, float, string, binary, array, ordered arbitrary-key maps, and raw extensions. Collections/binary inputs are copied and reading is through pattern matching or exhaustive typed `Match`.

Generated typed `*Async` methods live directly on the partial `NvimClient`. Buffer, Window, and Tabpage are immutable client-independent handles passed explicitly to overloads. Only non-deprecated metadata is generated; unsupported `LuaRef` functions produce visible diagnostics.

The current 69 CLR UI events become generated `NvimUiEvent` record cases delivered as ordered redraw batches through one registration API.

## Generator architecture

`Nvim.Client.Generator` owns supplied-input metadata/documentation readers, an immutable neutral `ApiDefinition`, recursive API types, validation/diagnostics, `IApiEmitter`, `GeneratedFileSet`, and the C# emitter. The neutral model contains no RPC envelope, runtime codec, Roslyn node, filesystem, process, or C# declaration model.

`Nvim.Client.Generator.Cli` owns arguments, launching `nvim --api-info`, optional Doxygen acquisition, filesystem output, diagnostics, and exit codes.

`IApiEmitter.Emit(ApiDefinition)` returns a deterministic `GeneratedFileSet`. The C# emitter builds declarations with Roslyn 5.6.0 `SyntaxFactory`, then CSharpier 1.3.0 is the final formatter. There is no plugin registry, DI framework, Workspaces/source-generator infrastructure, or speculative F# emitter.

Generated files stay tracked under the runtime project, so ordinary builds need neither Neovim nor Doxygen. Tests use focused metadata/documentation fixtures, representative generated compilation, semantic assertions, and one compact formatting golden rather than a full live-metadata snapshot.

## Delivery

The branch will contain three buildable logical commits:

1. neutral model, Roslyn emitter, CLI split, and generator fixtures;
2. `NvimValue`, RPC runtime/lifecycle, generated client surface, deletion of both old runtime projects, and minimum solution/test rewiring needed to stay buildable;
3. final solution/test renames, workflows, README/package metadata, local single-package proof, and deletion audit.

Review corrections will be amended into their owning logical commit rather than appended as fixups. Final verification includes wire/protocol/lifecycle/concurrency tests, owned/borrowed resource behavior, handler isolation and re-entrancy, ordered UI batches, real-Neovim request/inbound-handler/stdio/address paths, Roslyn compilation, CSharpier, all-target build/tests, local pack of exactly `Nvim.Client`, source-size ceilings, and zero legacy path/namespace/reference hits.

This PR will close #31, #35, and #40. It will not publish a package or absorb #36's release/version policy.

title: proposal: Re-architect RPC client generator around neutral model and emitter abstraction + Roslyn
